newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - February 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - February 3.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Monday.
- Irish coalition government's policies on crime fail to win majority support in poll.
- Hospital consultants on Sunday defended VHI fee increases of more than 130 percent in the past six years.
- British government scientists have warned that the proposed first underground nuclear waste dump at Sellafield could leak radioactivity into Cumbria and the Irish sea.
- Tens of thousands of people took part in a march in Derry on Sunday to commemorate the 25th anniversay of the Bloody Sunday killing.

- Ulster Unionist MPs have been to the Foreign Office in London to complain about the "activities" of Ireland's President Mary Robinson in Northern Ireland and later this week the British foreign secretary Malcolm Rifkind will receive a report outlining their "concerns".

- German and French officials have sought at the Davos summit to defuse a row over the European cental bank's independence and agreed it would be immune from political pressure when the single currency starts in 1999.
- The names of all politicians listed in the report on payments by Dunnes Stores are expected to be published this week.
- The government is losing the battle on crime, a new poll reveals and it could cost the coalition the next election.
- The Irish government is stepping up its opposition to British plans for an underground nuclear waste dump at Sellafield as two new studies cast further doubts about its safety.
- The EU's infamous beef mountain is set to make a comeback following the fall in markets in the wake of shoppers' fears about BSE.

- Irish Life will begin suspending staff today in its dispute with up to 400 sales workers, following a vote by members of the MSF union to reject a one million Irish pound Labour Court settlement package.
- Millions of pounds in investments and hundreds of Irish jobs are under threat as Germany prepares a bid to shut down offshore tax havens including Dublin's International Financial Services Centre.
- June 11 and 12 are the most likely dates for the general election, following the big rise in coalition support in the latest opinion poll.
- The Irish stock market should out-perform international markets in 1997, according to BCP Stockbrokckers and Fuund Managers.
